intro.h2: An East Bay team that plans every detail before demo day
paragraphs: HDR Remodeling has handled kitchen remodeling in Berkeley, Oakland and the nearby East Bay since 1987. The firm's architect, designers, estimator, project managers and carpenters all work for HDR, so the people who draw your kitchen are the people who build it. Many of the homes it works on are older, and the team aims to add modern function without losing their character.

HDR's process is built to keep the build short. Materials are ordered after you sign, and construction does not begin until every item is on the job site and inspected. A lead carpenter is on site each day, and the head of production checks in about every other day and every Friday.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Berkeley, plus baths, ADUs and whole homes

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Custom kitchens planned around how you cook and gather, from galley kitchens in Berkeley bungalows to open kitchens with islands in Oakland. HDR's NARI award list includes Regional Contractor of the Year kitchen wins in 2020 and 2023.

image.alt: Berkeley kitchen remodel with blue-painted cabinets, white subway tile, a range hood in the same blue and an island with black stools

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary baths, guest baths and new bathrooms added where none existed. Designers handle tile, vanities and fixtures, and the build team installs them to the approved plans. Recent baths range from Berkeley and Albany to Piedmont, Oakland and Kensington.

image.alt: Berkeley bathroom remodel with teal glossy wall tile, frameless glass shower, walnut vanity and floating orange shelves

items.name: Whole-Home and Historic Remodels
items.blurb: Kitchen, dining, living and bedroom remodels that open older floor plans while keeping original details. The design team specializes in historic Bay Area homes and works with an in-house California licensed architect to solve technically challenging layouts.

image.alt: Oakland whole-home remodel joining the kitchen and dining room, with a round wood table, black spindle chairs and an open staircase

items.name: ADUs and Garage Conversions
items.blurb: Backyard ADUs, studio offices and garage conversions planned with HDR's in-house architect, designers and builders. HDR won a Chrysalis Award for an ADU in 2019, and a recent blog post covers a Berkeley garage turned into a multi-use room.

image.alt: Backyard office ADU in Oakland with navy siding, white French doors and a wood ceiling over the entry

items.name: Basements, Attics and Outdoor Living
items.blurb: Unused basements and attics turned into living space, plus decks, patios and outdoor kitchens from HDR's landscape design-build team. Each one follows the same design, permit and build steps HDR uses for a kitchen or bath.

image.alt: Oakland attic conversion bedroom with exposed wood beams, a skylight, a paper pendant lamp and a wood bed frame

why_choose_us.h2: How HDR keeps East Bay remodels on track

items.title: No start until materials arrive
items.text: HDR orders materials once you sign and does not begin construction until every item is on the job site and inspected, so you are not living in a construction zone any longer than needed.

items.title: Someone on site every day
items.text: Your Lead Carpenter is on site daily unless you are told otherwise. The Head of Production reviews progress about every other day and always on Friday, and you get weekly progress reports.

items.title: A long record of NARI awards
items.text: The awards page lists NARI Regional Contractor of the Year wins for kitchens and baths in 2020 and 2023, an addition in 2024, a Chrysalis Award and a GuildQuality Guildmaster with Distinction.

items.title: A warranty past the industry standard
items.text: HDR's Peace of Mind warranty coverage extends well beyond the industry-standard warranty period, and every job ends with a thorough walkthrough before you sign off.

about.text: Chris Fellows is President of HDR Remodeling and has been with the company since 2009. He brings 25 years of construction experience and holds California B General Building and C-6 Cabinet and Finish Carpentry licenses. He is a NARI Certified Remodeling Project Manager, Lead R&R certified and C2 asbestos safety certified. Chris directs HDR's trades, vendors and suppliers alongside Vice President Kevin Mond, who is usually the first person new clients meet. Licensed architect Milton Tong and design manager Tamar Nachshon lead design, and production manager Alberto Navarro Ruiz runs the build crews.

image.alt: Chris Fellows, President of HDR Remodeling in Emeryville, CA

steps.title: In-home consultation
steps.text: A complimentary visit to review your wish list and walk the project. HDR suggests starting a Houzz ideabook to share the looks you like.

steps.title: Studio meeting
steps.text: A complimentary meeting at the office and design studio to explore options and estimated cost ranges, and sign a design agreement if you both agree.

steps.title: Design and permits
steps.text: A Design + Build Coordinator schedules design meetings, schematic drawings and cost estimates. After the contract, HDR files for building permits and zoning approval.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Materials arrive and are inspected first. A Pass the Baton meeting hands your job from design to production, then your Lead Carpenter works on site daily.

steps.title: Walk-through and photos
steps.text: A personal post-production walk-through lets you review and sign off on the work, followed by a professional photo shoot of the finished space.

service_area.h2: Serving Berkeley, Oakland and the inner East Bay
service_area.text: HDR works from its office and design studio on Horton Street in Emeryville. The site names Alameda, Albany, Berkeley, El Cerrito, Kensington, Oakland and Piedmont as its core service area. The project gallery shows kitchens and baths on Berkeley streets like Virginia, Hopkins and Grizzly Peak, Oakland homes in Rockridge, and finished work in Alameda, Albany, El Cerrito, Kensington and Piedmont.

faq.h2: Common questions from Berkeley and Oakland homeowners

items.a: Yes. HDR starts with a complimentary visit to your home to review your wish list and walk the space. Next comes a complimentary meeting at its office and design studio, where you look at design options and estimated cost ranges. Most clients sign a design agreement at that meeting if both sides want to go ahead.

items.q: Why won't construction start right after I sign?
items.a: HDR orders your materials once the contract is signed and the deposit is in, and it does not start work until all of them are on the job site and inspected. That way your kitchen or bath is not torn apart while you wait on a late cabinet or tile delivery.

items.q: Who will be at my house during the build?
items.a: Your assigned Lead Carpenter is on site every day unless you are told otherwise. The Head of Production visits about every other day and always on Friday. You also get weekly progress reports and access to HDR's project management software to track milestones and selections.

items.q: Can you update an older home without losing its character?
items.a: That is a focus for HDR. Its design team specializes in historic Bay Area homes and aims to keep each home's character while adding modern function. One Berkeley client wrote that the team kept the style and sensibility of their bungalow while bringing in new ideas.

items.q: Do you handle permits and offer a warranty?
items.a: Yes. After the construction contract is signed, HDR files for building permits and zoning approval. When the job is done, a walkthrough confirms every detail, and HDR's Peace of Mind warranty coverage extends well beyond the industry-standard warranty period for your remodel.
